Triage (daily round, session `session_01Kktexqp6uVuFMztvvTMf3V`, 2026-08-24): lands in `app-shell` `defaultMapFromObject` → `domain:ui` + `pm:queue`, Bug — derive a marker-title binding like every sibling deriver (display-field heuristic), so interface-page maps stop falling back to a literal `name`. Family: objectui#5908 (merged), objectstack#11443/#11442. Serial note: re-verify `InterfaceListPage.tsx` on current main (post-#5908) before editing.

Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`
Clause-②: no — a derivation gains a field it already had the inputs for; no authoring key changes and no published surface widens.
Serial constraints cleared: `packages/app-shell/src/views/InterfaceListPage.tsx` — no in-flight claim touches it; zero `claude/issue-*` branches on the remote. ⚠️ Sibling card **#5522** runs concurrently inside `packages/app-shell` but in `src/observability/sentry.ts` — a **different file in a different directory**; surfaces are disjoint by full path, not by basename.

## Premise verified by this seat before dispatch — but re-verify, do not trust me

`defaultMapFromObject` on current `origin/main` reads, in full:

```ts
export function defaultMapFromObject(objectDef: any): { locationField: string } | undefined {
  const field =
    firstFieldMatching(objectDef, (_n, f) => LOCATION_TYPES.has(f.type)) ??
    firstFieldMatching(objectDef, (n) => /location|address|geo|coords?|place|venue/i.test(n));
  return field ? { locationField: field } : undefined;
}
```

So the return type carries **no** title binding — the card's claim stands as of dispatch.

⚠️ **This file moved twice in the last day** — `#5860` (`derive ObjectSchemaMetadata from the spec's ServiceObject`, 01:13Z) and `#5908` (`read the spec's view-level map block on list views`, which closed #5042). **#5908 is adjacent to this card's subject**: it made the view-level `map` block reach plugin-map. Re-read the landed shape of both before writing, and note that the call site at ~:361 now reads `(view.options as any)?.map ?? (allowedSet.has('map') ? defaultMapFromObject(objectDef) : undefined)` — an author-supplied `map` block takes precedence over the derivation, so establish **which path** produces the `undefined` titles the card reports before fixing either.

## What "like every sibling deriver" has to mean

The card's whole argument is that this deriver is the odd one out. ⛔ Do not take that on faith — **locate the sibling derivers and state what they actually bind**, then match that convention rather than inventing one. If the siblings disagree with each other, say so and pick with a reason; that is a finding worth more than a guess.

The failure the user sees is `undefined` marker titles whenever the display field is not `name`, so the fix has to consult the object's **display field**, not hardcode `name`. Pin the not-`name` case specifically — a test on an object whose display field *is* `name` would pass on the defect.

Run `packages/app-shell` tests **path-filtered** — the whole-package suite is ~784 s and holds the shared verify lock (seat post §5).

## ACCEPT — PR #5955, pending CI convergence

Reviewed against GitHub, not against the report's self-account. Landing waits on the gate read.

### Checklist

| item | reading |
|---|---|
| PR form | draft ✓, base `main` ✓, `Fixes #5909` ✓ |
| Scope vs. declared fence | 3 files, **exactly** the fence: `InterfaceListPage.tsx`, `InterfaceListPage.mapConfig.test.tsx`, one changeset. No breach. |
| Changeset | present, `patch` for `@object-ui/app-shell`, and it describes the user-visible symptom rather than the edit |
| Cross-package import | `deriveTitleField` from `@object-ui/core` — app-shell already declares that dependency; `check-phantom-dependencies` green |
| CI | still converging at review time — **not yet read** |

### The PM assumption this card was dispatched on was wrong, and saying so is the most valuable thing in the PR

I briefed this as *"the card's whole argument is that this deriver is the odd one out — locate the siblings and state what they actually bind."* The dev did, and the answer falsifies the card's framing: **no sibling deriver binds a title.** `kanban → groupByField`, `calendar → startDateField`, `gallery → coverField`, `gantt → start/end/progress?` — each binds its own required field and stops, and `defaultMapFromObject` bound `locationField`, *its* required field. By the card's own measure, map was never the odd one out.

The real asymmetry sits one layer down, at the renderers: `ObjectKanban:301`, `ObjectCalendar:356` and `ObjectGantt:600` resolve titles through `@object-ui/core#getRecordDisplayName` (ADR-0079) and need nothing derived; `ObjectMap` never imports the resolver and reads `record[titleField]` bare against a literal `'name'` default. **That is a better diagnosis than the card's, and it changes what the fix means** — this PR closes the interface-page seam and explicitly declines to claim the general fix, which is filed as #5953.

### Two checks that separate this from a plausible-looking version of itself

- **`titleField` is on `FLAT_MAP_CONFIG_KEYS`.** The derived key has to survive `pickFlatMapConfig`'s whitelisted flatten to reach `getMapConfig`. A key outside that list would have made the entire change a **silent no-op** — green tests, unchanged product. Verifying the key is on the whitelist is the difference between a fix and a decoration.
- **The path with the defect was established before it was fixed.** Both the authored `options.map` bag and the derivation converge on the same flat branch; the authored block can declare `titleField` and the derivation could not, so the derivation is the path carrying the unavoidable defect. Fixing the other one would have shipped a green no-op.

### Test quality

- The **anti-drift arm** is the strongest piece: it asserts `record[derivedTitleField] === getRecordDisplayName(objectDef, record)` across four object shapes, so a map and a kanban over one object cannot disagree about what a record is called. It is also honestly scoped — `titleFormat` and the record-key probe are declared out of reach for a static field-name binding rather than silently skipped.
- **Controls are present and their weakness is named.** The `display field IS name` arm would pass on the defect, and the test says so in a comment rather than letting it pad the count.
- **`nameField` is proven load-bearing** rather than decorative: the fixture ranks `title` above `headline` in the bare scan, so an implementation calling only `deriveTitleField` answers `headline`-less and fails that arm.
- **Omitted, not fabricated** — when nothing resolves the key is absent, so a derived value can never be mistaken for a declared choice at the read site.
- The **second reverse-check** is a nice touch: pasting a type the real signature must reject turned `tsc` red by name (`TS2322`), proving the new cross-package import is genuinely type-checked and not silently `any`.

### Reuse over reimplementation

`deriveTitleField` is **imported** from `@object-ui/core`, not copied. Given this lane's standing burn-down of hand-copied field-family tables (#5874, #5875, #5692), a private re-ranking here would have been a new copy to retire later. Correct call.

### One note for triage, not a defect in this PR

**#5953** is filed unassigned with `domain:ui` but **no `finding` label and no pm-state**. That is the half-labelled shape the triage sweep's case ③ is designed to catch, so it will be seen — but its sibling #5954 was filed with `finding` + `domain:ui`. Flagging the inconsistency for first touch; ⛔ not grading it here.
